root_motivation: Grounding (PRD): run-result-overflow-to-state AC10 failed live on prod 0.60.18 (run 244, runs/244/live/ac10.md §4): /var/lib/mcphost/plans.toml on mcphost-1 predates tenant state and has no state_* lines; PlanBuilder::build (src/plans.rs ~616-630) filled state_bytes_max, state_rows_max, state_ops_per_call_max with unwrap_or(0) while every sibling field fell back to its documented default -- so every tenant on both plans had state_bytes_max == 0 and every state write, table overflow, and run-result overflow on prod failed with state_quota. Nothing in the code, the deploy, or healthz said so; a live AC verifier found it by reading the box file, and the operator hand-patched it 2026-09-26.
user_persona: Three (PRD User stories): (1) an operator (Joe) who upgrades mcphost across ten releases without touching plans.toml, expecting every new quota to be live at its documented default; (2) an agent on the free plan whose host.state.set of 4 KiB must succeed on a fresh prod tenant even when the box's plans.toml predates that quota; (3) an instrument (synthorg) that reads healthz.plans and asserts a quota is non-zero before scoring a stateful task.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a plans.toml with free and pro naming only price_usd_month, tools_max, calls_per_day, secrets_max, description, When the catalog loads, Then free.state_bytes_max == 5 MiB, free.state_rows_max == 10000, pro.state_bytes_max == 200 MiB, and every other quota equals default_catalog()'s value for that plan.
Given that file, When the host starts, Then the log contains "plans.toml: plan=free defaulted=[" naming state_bytes_max and "plans.toml: plan=pro defaulted=[".
Given a plan named team naming only tools_max, When it loads, Then its unnamed quotas equal the free plan's defaults and the log line names plan team.
Given the loaded catalog, When admin healthz is read, Then plans[] lists each plan with the six quota fields and non-zero state_bytes_max.
Given a plans.toml produced by to_toml() of the default catalog, When it loads, Then the catalog is byte-for-byte equal to default_catalog() and no defaulted= line is logged.
Given src/plans.rs after this PRD, When grepped, Then no quota field in PlanBuilder::build uses unwrap_or(0) or a numeric literal (test reads the source file).
Given www/llms.txt, When the operator notes are read, Then they name the defaulting behavior and the startup line.

Given prod after deploy with the operator-provisioned 2026-09-26 plans.toml still in place, When admin healthz is read through https://mcphost.dev/healthz with the admin key from orch ~/.config/mcphost/admin-key, Then plans[0].state_bytes_max == 5242880 and host.state.set of a 4 KiB value on the operator tenant returns ok (Live; evidence: healthz version after deploy plus the call transcript this AC names, saved under docs/receipts/<slug>.md).
acceptance_criteria.test: deferred: operator-provisioned -- needs a real deploy to https://mcphost.dev, an admin key from orch's local config, and prod access this coding sandbox cannot produce; AC1-AC6's branch-local tests prove the always-on defaulting mechanism AC8's live check depends on.

scope: src/plans.rs: PlanBuilder::build takes the loading plan's own default_catalog() row (by name, free for an unrecognized name) instead of a per-field literal, and returns which fields it filled in; PlanCatalog::from_toml resolves that default row per [[plan]] via a new finalize_plan helper and returns the per-plan defaulted-field report alongside the catalog; PlanCatalog::load_or_init logs one plans.toml: plan=<name> defaulted=[...] INFO line per plan with at least one defaulted field.
src/http.rs: admin healthz's body gains plans: [{name, state_bytes_max, state_rows_max, table_bytes_max, docs_bytes_max, jobs_concurrent, end_users_max}] from state.plans.
www/llms.txt: Operator notes gains one sentence naming the defaulting behavior and the plans.toml: plan=<name> defaulted=[...] startup line.
non_goals: Rewriting the operator's plans.toml on disk -- only absent fields are filled at load time; an operator's explicit values stay authoritative and the file itself is never touched.
New quotas or plan tiers -- this PRD only fixes how an already-declared quota defaults when a hand-edited or old file omits it.

A real prod deploy or live healthz/host.state.set transcript against mcphost.dev -- AC8 is deferred operator-provisioned; only the always-on defaulting mechanism (AC1-AC6) and the healthz surface (AC4) are built branch-local.

additional.default_lookup_by_name_not_always_free: requirement 1 explicitly resolves the loading plan's OWN row in default_catalog() by name (free only as the fallback for a name default_catalog() doesn't have) -- a pro row missing state_bytes_max must default to pro's 200 MiB, not free's 5 MiB, which is exactly the shape the prior unwrap_or(0)/unwrap_or(<free's literal>) code got wrong.
additional.no_rewrite_of_the_on_disk_file: load_or_init only writes plans.toml when the path does not exist yet (AC1's fresh-data-dir seed); a file that already exists is read and its defaulted fields filled in memory only -- never written back.
additional.defaulted_report_empty_means_silent: finalize_plan only pushes a plan into the defaulted-fields report when at least one of its Option<i64> fields was None, so a fully-named file (AC5) logs nothing.

five_whys_trace.q: Why did every tenant's state_bytes_max end up 0 on prod instead of some wrong-but-nonzero number?
five_whys_trace.a: PlanBuilder::build's three state_* fields used .unwrap_or(0) -- a literal, not a lookup -- while every sibling quota field added by a later PRD (concurrent_calls_per_tenant, table_bytes_max, job_max_s, ...) already fell back to that PRD's own documented default; state_bytes_max/state_rows_max/state_ops_per_call_max were added without that same tolerant-parse treatment.

five_whys_trace.q: Why did nothing in the code, the deploy, or healthz catch a quota silently at 0?
five_whys_trace.a: from_toml had no notion of 'which fields did I just default' to log, and healthz exposed no per-plan quota view at all -- the only way to see the bug was to read the box's own plans.toml file by hand, which is exactly how the live AC verifier found it.

five_whys_trace.q: Why generalize this to every quota field (requirement 1) instead of just fixing the three state_* fields?
five_whys_trace.a: The technical considerations section names the root cause directly: 'the duplicated literals are how the siblings drifted from the catalog' -- the defaults already exist once, in default_catalog(); any field defaulted by a literal in PlanBuilder::build (not just the three that just broke) is one more release away from the same silent-zero failure the next time a sibling default changes.

five_whys_trace.q: Why fall back to the loading plan's OWN default_catalog() row (by name) instead of always falling back to free's row, the way most of the pre-existing per-field comments described?
five_whys_trace.a: AC1 requires pro.state_bytes_max == 200 MiB when pro's own plans.toml row never named it -- a fixed always-free fallback would give pro the free plan's 5 MiB, wrong for the exact plan the bug report was about.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does an unrecognized plan name (AC3's team) fall back to free rather than erroring or using some other default?
five_whys_trace.a: Requirement 1 states the fallback explicitly ('or, for an unknown plan name, the free plan's value') -- a plan the operator has hand-added under a name default_catalog() doesn't know still needs to load with some sane, documented quota set rather than failing load_or_init outright.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Requirement 2 says from_toml 'returns, alongside the catalog, the list of (plan, field) pairs it defaulted' -- does that mean from_toml's own public return type changes, or does load_or_init log without changing from_toml's signature?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: from_toml's signature changed to Result<(Self, Vec<(String, Vec<String>)>), AppError> -- no caller outside plans.rs existed (grepped before changing it), so this is free; load_or_init (the one startup call site, per requirement 2's own 'startup logs' wording) unwraps the tuple and does the actual tracing::info! logging, keeping its own external signature (Result<Self, AppError>) unchanged for main.rs and every existing test.
